nodes.label: curriculum schema
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL mirror of the Neo4j curriculum graph, used for RLS-controlled reads and as the source for graph writes; the Neo4j graph is derived from these tables, not the other way around.

nodes.label: ministry schema
nodes.rationale: Ministry-level data is always anonymised; only accessible by the ministry role and contains no individual student identifiers.

nodes.label: audit schema
nodes.rationale: Immutable audit trail; rows are INSERT-only, append-only enforced by GRANT (no UPDATE/DELETE granted to application roles).

nodes.label: embeddings schema (pgvector)
nodes.rationale: Stores vector embeddings for semantic similarity search used for CLO-to-question matching and topic-to-CLO alignment; requires the pgvector extension (CREATE EXTENSION vector).

nodes.label: curriculum.topics table
nodes.rationale: Central to the entire system — every other table references topics directly or indirectly.

nodes.label: curriculum.topic_prerequisites table
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL mirror of the Neo4j PREREQUISITE_OF relationships, used for RLS queries and sync validation; the Neo4j graph remains the authoritative traversal store.

nodes.label: curriculum.clos table
nodes.rationale: Authoritative source for Curriculum Learning Outcomes, uploaded from the official MOE CLO document.

nodes.label: curriculum.topic_clo_mappings table
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE constraint on (topic_id, clo_code) — a topic-CLO pair is mapped exactly once; match method and score stored for auditability.

nodes.label: assessment.student_answers table
nodes.rationale: PARTITIONED BY LIST (school_id) at national scale to keep all answers for a school co-located; expected ~5.2B rows/year (26M students x ~50 answers/exam x 4 exams/year). Most heavily written table in the system.

nodes.label: students.student_profiles table
nodes.rationale: Shares its primary key (1:1) with identity.users. PII fields (national_id, date_of_birth, parent_contact) are AES-256-GCM encrypted at the application layer to satisfy Ministry data-protection requirements.

nodes.label: students.gap_records table
nodes.rationale: Persisted output of the gap analysis engine, one row per topic per student, updated after each exam attempt.

nodes.label: students.mastery_records table
nodes.rationale: Set when a student passes questions for all CLOs of a topic across >=2 exams (positive mastery).

nodes.label: schools.quality_scores table
nodes.rationale: Nightly-computed composite quality score per school, per subject, per grade.

nodes.label: regions.regional_aggregates table
nodes.rationale: Pre-computed regional performance summaries, updated nightly by a Celery batch job.

nodes.label: ministry.curriculum_change_log table
nodes.rationale: Every change to CLOs, topic structures, or prerequisites is logged here for policy audit.

nodes.label: audit.access_log table
nodes.rationale: No RLS — super_admin only via GRANT; no application role has INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.

nodes.label: audit.data_change_log table
nodes.rationale: Trigger-maintained; every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on student_answers, gap_records, mastery_records, and exam_attempts creates a row here.

nodes.label: audit.ai_request_log table
nodes.rationale: Stores only a SHA-256 prompt_hash — prompt content is never stored, for privacy.

nodes.label: embeddings.clo_embeddings table
nodes.rationale: Indexed with HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World), preferred over IVFFlat for production because it maintains accuracy during online inserts without requiring periodic index rebuilds.

nodes.label: embeddings.question_embeddings table
nodes.rationale: Indexed with HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World), preferred over IVFFlat for production because it maintains accuracy during online inserts without requiring periodic index rebuilds.

nodes.label: (:Topic) Neo4j node label
nodes.rationale: Most important node in the graph.

nodes.label: (:Student) Neo4j node label
nodes.rationale: Lightweight mirror for traversal only — full student data lives in PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: (:Region) Neo4j node label
nodes.rationale: Implied by the (School)-[:IN_REGION]->(Region) relationship and the idx_school_region index; not given its own properties table in section 3.1, unlike the other node labels.

nodes.label: [:HAS_SUBTOPIC] relationship
nodes.rationale: Subtopics are also Topic nodes — self-referential relationship on (:Topic).

nodes.label: [:PREREQUISITE_OF] relationship
nodes.rationale: Self-referential Topic->Topic edge; walked upstream 1..5 hops for gap-analysis root-cause chains. idx_topic_prereq_grade optimises cross-grade traversal.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 16 (AWS RDS af-south-1)
nodes.rationale: System of record for all transactional, ACID-compliant data. Organised into 14 schemas; RLS enabled on every table containing student or school data; all PKs UUID v4; all timestamps TIMESTAMPTZ (UTC).

nodes.label: Neo4j 5.x Enterprise (AuraDB af-south-1)
nodes.rationale: Owns the curriculum knowledge graph and all relationship-traversal intelligence (subjects, topics, CLOs, questions, prerequisites, careers). Populated from PostgreSQL via logical replication, not the system of record.

nodes.label: Redis 7 (ElastiCache af-south-1)
nodes.rationale: Owns ephemeral state: sessions, API response caches, Bull MQ job queues, WebSocket pub-sub, rate-limit counters. maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru; AOF disabled since cache data is recreatable.

nodes.label: AWS S3 (af-south-1)
nodes.rationale: Owns binary objects (curriculum PDFs, exam files, submission scans, reports, model artifacts, audit logs). Access only via presigned URLs from the Go API; frontend never holds permanent AWS credentials. Block Public Access enabled on all buckets.

nodes.label: Bull MQ job queues (bull:*)
nodes.rationale: Key patterns managed internally by Bull MQ via Redis sorted sets and lists — do not write to these keys directly.

nodes.label: edugraph-model-artifacts S3 bucket
nodes.rationale: Public-read via CloudFront since Ollama model files are not PII.

nodes.label: edugraph-audit-logs S3 bucket
nodes.rationale: Object Lock (Governance mode), 7-year retention, WORM — immutability required for compliance audit trail.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL to Neo4j sync worker
nodes.rationale: A Go worker subscribes to a PostgreSQL logical replication slot (pglogrepl) and processes row-level changes, writing corresponding Neo4j Cypher MERGE operations. At-least-once delivery with idempotent MERGE; neo4j_written flag tracks success; failures retry via Bull MQ with exponential backoff (1s,4s,16s,64s) before going to a dead-letter queue after 5 failures. The same pattern runs on School Boxes via ElectricSQL to cloud PostgreSQL, then the cloud worker propagates to Neo4j.

nodes.label: Four-store polyglot persistence strategy
nodes.rationale: EduGraph AI uses four data stores, each chosen for what it does best — no single database does everything. Graph-shaped data (topics, CLOs, prerequisites, student mastery) lives in Neo4j; data requiring joins/FKs/transactions (grades, enrollments, users) lives in PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Neo4j graph derived from PostgreSQL, not authoritative
nodes.rationale: Every Neo4j node is first written to PostgreSQL; Neo4j is populated by a sync worker consuming PostgreSQL logical replication events. Neo4j is the traversal engine, PostgreSQL is the system of record.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL-Neo4j eventual consistency model
nodes.rationale: Neo4j lags PostgreSQL by 0-30 seconds in normal operation. Gap analysis and study plan generation check a lag counter; if Neo4j is more than 2 minutes behind, the API returns 503 with Retry-After rather than serving stale results.

nodes.label: Backward-compatible migration rules
nodes.rationale: Never DROP a column (rename via alias pattern instead); never rename a table (add a VIEW with the old name); new NOT NULL columns must have a DEFAULT; FK additions must be NOT VALID first then validated separately; all Neo4j schema migrations must be additive (MERGE not REPLACE) using OPTIONAL MATCH for new properties. Managed by Flyway (PostgreSQL) and a custom Cypher migration runner (Neo4j) — no schema change may be applied manually.

nodes.label: Row-Level Security as last line of defence
nodes.rationale: Even a misconfigured application query cannot return cross-tenant data because PostgreSQL enforces RLS policies at the engine level. The Go API middleware sets session-local variables (app.current_user_id, app.current_school_id, app.current_region_id, app.current_role) before every DB operation, and RLS policies read these variables.
